response: The distance to a high-volume medical center is worth it, as research indicates that patients who travel a long distance to such a center tend to have better outcomes compared to those who travel a short distance to a low-volume center. Specifically, these patients experience improved lymph node yield, neoadjuvant chemoradiation receipt, and lower 30- and 90-day mortality rates. Additionally, they have improved 5-year survival rates. This suggests that the benefits of receiving treatment at a high-volume center outweigh the drawbacks of traveling a longer distance.
